body.text: Global supply chains and geopolitical balances increasingly pivot around Zohran Mamdani. Tracking the primary facts helps separate durable structural shifts from daily noise.

Zohran Kwame Mamdani (born October 18, 1991) is an American politician serving as the 112th mayor of New York City since 2026. A member of the Democratic Party and the Democratic Socialists of America, he represented the 36th district in the New York State Assembly from 2021 to 2025.
Mamdani is New York City's first Muslim mayor and its first Asian American mayor.

Mamdani was born in Kampala, Uganda, to film director Mira Nair and political scientist Mahmood Mamdani, both of Indian descent. He moved to New York City at age seven and graduated from Bowdoin College in 2014 with a bachelor's degree in Africana studies. After graduation, he worked as a housing counselor and rapper.

He entered New York City politics as a volunteer for Ali Najmi's 2015 City Council campaign, and later managed Ross Barkan's 2018 State Senate campaign. He was first elected to the New York State Assembly in 2020, defeating five-term incumbent Aravella Simotas in the Democratic primary.
Representing Astoria and Long Island City, he was reelected without opposition in 2022 and 2024.

In October 2024, Mamdani announced his candidacy for mayor of New York City in the 2025 mayoral election. A democratic socialist, Mamdani campaigned on a progressive, affordability-focused platform, supporting fare-free city buses, universal child care, city-owned grocery stores, a rent freeze on rent-stabilized units, additional affordable housing units, and a $30 minimum wage by 2030.

He also expressed support for LGBTQ rights, comprehensive public safety reform, and tax increases on corporations and those earning more than $1 million a year. He won the Democratic primary in June 2025, defeating former governor Andrew Cuomo in an upset.
He was elected mayor in the November general election, defeating Cuomo, who ran as an independent, and Republican Curtis Sliwa.

As mayor, Mamdani has focused on affordability. In January 2026, he and Governor Kathy Hochul announced a plan to expand free child care, and in June the Rent Guidelines Board approved a freeze on rents for rent-stabilized apartments. Mamdani's administration has also named the first site for a planned network of city-owned grocery stores.

His tenure has included conflicts with the Trump administration over immigration enforcement, court challenges to his pied-à-terre tax, and criticism from some Jewish organizations and elected officials over his positions on Israel. Mamdami has repeatedly condemned antisemitism and has pledged millions of dollars to fight antisemitic hate crimes in New York City.

Mamdani's mayoral victory challenged the centrist establishment of the Democratic Party and presaged a wave of progressive and leftist victories in state and federal elections in 2026. Increasingly, he is viewed as a power broker within the party, and is credited with promoting candidates who unseated several Democratic incumbents in New York's federal congressional caucus.
Early life and education

Zohran Kwame Mamdani was born on October 18, 1991, at Nsambya Hospital in Kampala, Uganda. He is the only child of the postcolonialist academic Mahmood Mamdani and the filmmaker Mira Nair, who are both of Indian descent.

His father is a Gujarati Muslim from Mumbai who was raised in Uganda in the Khoja Twelver community, itself a part of the Indian diaspora in East Africa. His mother is a Punjabi Hindu who was born in Rourkela, in the Indian state of Odisha, and raised in Delhi.
Mamdani was given his middle name, Kwame, by his father in honor of Kwame Nkrumah, the first president of Ghana.

When Mamdani was five, his family moved to Cape Town, South Africa, after his father was appointed head of African studies at the University of Cape Town. George's Grammar School in Mowbray from 1996 to 1998, during the early post-apartheid years.

He later said that living in Cape Town taught him "what inequality looks like up close... that justice has to be more than an idea, it has to be material". When Mamdani was seven, the family moved to the United States and settled in the Morningside Heights neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City.

Mamdani attended the Bank Street School for Children on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, where he won a mock presidential election at the age of 12. His platform included "equal rights" and a proposal to spend money on education rather than the military.

After spending a year in Kampala during his father's sabbatical, Mamadani attended the Bronx High School of Science in the Bronx, where he co-founded the school's first cricket team and unsuccessfully ran for student body vice president.

Mamdani attended Bowdoin College in Brunswick, Maine, where he co-founded the school's chapter of Students for Justice in Palestine and was a regular contributor to the campus newspaper The Bowdoin Orient. In 2014, he co-authored an op-ed in the Bangor Daily News urging Bowdoin to join the American Studies Association's boycott of Israel.
Music career

Mamdani has produced and performed rap music. He and the Ugandan rapper HAB (Abdul Bar Hussein) performed as the duo Young Cardamom & HAB in Uganda. Their first song, "Kanda ", is about the Indian flatbread chapati, which is a staple food in Uganda.

According to Mamdani, the song features lyrics in multiple languages, including English, Luganda, Nubi and Swahili, to express the belief that residents of Uganda with roots in other countries should be considered Ugandan.

At the 2016 Nyege Nyege music festival in Jinja, they performed tracks from their EP Sidda Mukyaalo (Luganda: 'No going back to the village'), which was released that year. In their music, they addressed social issues in Uganda, such as corruption and "black and brown relations", as well as colonialism.
The duo were nominated for "Rookie of the Year" at the inaugural Uganda Hip Hop Awards.

Mamdani produced the soundtrack for the 2016 film Queen of Katwe, directed by his mother Mira Nair. He and HAB wrote the song "1 Spice" for the film, and Mamdani is credited as third assistant director. His work on the soundtrack earned him a nomination for the Guild of Music Supervisors Award in 2017.

Nair subsequently offered him roles in the stage musical adaptation of her film Monsoon Wedding and in her television adaptation of the Vikram Seth novel A Suitable Boy, but he declined both offers. In 2017, Mamdani released the song "Salaam" under the name Zohran Kwame. In 2019, under the moniker Mr.

Cardamom, he released the single "Nani", an homage to his grandmother. The actress and food writer Madhur Jaffrey plays the role of Mamdani's grandmother in the song's music video, which pays tribute to Jaffrey and New York's South Asian culture.
Early political career and advocacy

Mamdani entered New York City politics in 2015 as a volunteer for Ali Najmi's campaign in a special election for the 23rd district of the City Council. He became involved after discovering that Najmi was backed by Heems, a Das Racist co-founder and one of Mamdani's favorite rappers.

In 2017, Mamdani joined the New York City chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) and worked for the campaign of City Council candidate Khader El-Yateem, a Palestinian democratic socialist from Bay Ridge, Brooklyn. Part of Mamdani's motivation for joining the DSA was its pro-Palestine stance, which aligned with his own prior activism.

In 2018, he began working as a housing and foreclosure prevention counselor, helping lower-income immigrant homeowners in Queens avoid eviction. He managed Ross Barkan's unsuccessful 2018 campaign for the New York State Senate, and was a field organizer for Tiffany Cabán's narrowly unsuccessful 2019 campaign for Queens County district attorney.
New York State Assembly (2020, 2025)

In October 2019, Mamdani announced his campaign to represent New York's 36th State Assembly district, which encompasses Astoria and Long Island City in Queens. Endorsed by the DSA, he ran on a platform of housing reform, police and prison reform, and public ownership of utilities.

Mamdani's June 2020 primary victory over five-term Democratic incumbent Aravella Simotas took almost a month to call, and he won the general election with no Republican opposition in November. Mamdani was reelected without opposition in 2022 and 2024.
